notes.title: Character Spotlight: The Support
notes.content:
Don’t let the name fool you—Support isn’t here just to hand out water and psychological encouragement. This versatile class controls the battlefield like a boss!

With a knack for locking down space and buffing teammates at key moments, the Support doesn’t just assist—they set the pace, draw the lines, and in case you need that extra firepower is there to add some ranged damage for good measure.

[h2]Skills[/h2] 
[b]Minefield[/b]
Nothing screams “you shall not pass” like a freshly dropped minefield. Unless someone passes over it, in which case you can put on your sunglasses and deliver a punchy one liner.
Whether it’s cutting off flanking routes, protecting your squishier crew, or forcing enemies down a very painful hallway, this ability turns positioning into a win condition.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/9d374d88e3b879a36098074c36168a45751673a3.jpg[/img]

The Minefield is a draw skill, meaning you can hold your mouse over the grid until you have covered the area you want. After that you can focus on your positioning or any other objectives, having your bases covered! 
Disregard that I am trapping someones drying laundry in the picture above.

[b]Rile Up[/b]
Give your team the hype they need—a powerful buff that turns your next turn into a highlight reel. Time it right and you’ll see your crew explode with power, wiping the field before the enemy even knows what happened.
While the added Critical could possibly one-shot an adversary, the flat Power boost alone is worth it, especially when the buff is active for two turns. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/cbbd1238beb25b7e5866dbbde82d39beb11f98d4.jpg[/img]

Simply place the area over your crew and get ready for some serious damage, like it's no one's business! 

[b]Caravan Skill: Sharpen Senses[/b]
A crew that sees it coming is a crew that lives to tell the tale. Placing the Support on the back-line of your Caravan will unlock this powerful buff during combat for your front-liners. 
This team-wide buff massively boosts your dodge chance when it matters most. [strike]You might not always need it, but when you do..[/strike]—Trust me this is awesome, it’s a run-saver. 

    🛠️ Designer’s Note - Tasos: [i]The Support is one of those classes that just makes everything better. Lay down some mines, rile up your heavy hitters, and let the rest of the team follow your tempo. Whether you’re funneling enemies into traps or setting up a huge combo turn, this class is a tactical backbone.[/i]

So consider having a Support on your next run! Bring one along if you like winning!

notes.title: Character Spotlight: The Marine
notes.content:
Sometimes you don’t need a sniper or a hammer-swinging maniac. Sometimes you just need a Marine—reliable, tactical, and always ready to control the flow of combat with a grin.

This gun-wielding class brings mid-range firepower, mid-health durability, and enough crowd control to make you feel like you’re always one step ahead. The Marine won’t top the damage charts, but in the right hands? Oh, they’ll win you the fight.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/837e7eebc827bf0b5b0f4bfecf868a235c2d44a5.png[/img]

[h2]Skills[/h2] 
[b]Displacement Shot[/b]
It’s not just for laughs—this skill pushes enemies back, and if they hit something on the way (like a wall... or one of your Fire Pillars 👀), they take extra damage. It’s a positioning tool and a bonus damage dealer in one clean shot.

[b]Flashbang[/b]
This one’s for those crowded brawls—Area of Effect blind that makes enemies miss more. Works wonders when you’re surrounded or just want to give your brawlers a bit of breathing room.

[b]Caravan Skill: Spray and Pray[/b]
When you absolutely, positively need everything in front of you deleted—call in this AOE caravan attack. It’s not subtle, but it doesn’t have to be.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/1ef6884fecb635629760d5489312d7e5670412a5.png[/img]

🛠️ Designer’s Note - Tasos : [i]This one’s a personal favorite. The Displacement Shot → Fire Pillar combo is chef’s kiss—tactical, satisfying, and incredibly effective.[/i]

Whether you're pushing enemies into traps or blinding them before the real fight starts, the Marine has your back. Keep one in your squad—you’ll thank yourself later.

notes.title: 4 Combat Tips to Keep You (and Your Crew) Alive
notes.content:
So you’ve just stepped into the scorching sands, your ship’s barely holding together, and an angry Arcanist warband is charging your way—what now?

Combat in Dunebound Tactics isn’t about who has the biggest hammer/gun/staff (though, fair, some are very big), it’s about knowing when to strike, where to stand, and how to make every skill count. Here’s a quick rundown of 4 combat tips to help you survive your next firefight, ambush, or “oops this was supposed to be a peaceful negotiation” moment.

[h2]1. Prep Like a Pro[/h2]

The real fight starts before you enter combat.

Before the first rock gets thrown or explosive pillar gets summoned, ask yourself: does my squad actually work well together?

Build your crew with synergy in mind. A healer in your team can be the difference between limping into the Medbay or walking out with a smirk and full HP. Support characters with buffs, crowd control, or combo synergy can turn a desperate scrap into a clean sweep. Think of your team like a toolbox—if you only pack hammers, don’t be surprised when screws get the better of you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/a1d01e24d04393dfed9f10b1bebd4a99afe10807.png[/img]

[h2]2. Read the Room (and the Rocks)[/h2]

Not every battle is a punch-up.

Sometimes you’re defending an NPC. Sometimes you’re being picked apart by ranged enemies. Sometimes, it’s a full-on brawl in a dense cityscape. So your positioning needs to change with the situation.

Got melee enemies charging you? Get behind cover or funnel them into tight spaces. Need to protect someone important? Send your toughest fighter to body-block the heat. Don’t just charge in—adapt your formation to the field.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/07349672e6221745180953c0504a8d2791294ec2.png[/img]

[h2]3. Draw Skills = Big Brain Plays[/h2]

Despite the name, Draw skills aren’t about pulling enemies—they’re about placement.

Using your mouse, you’ll “draw” the layout of things like clusters of pillars, mines, or explosive lines, giving you the power to reshape the battlefield on your terms. Block a chokepoint. Cover your flank. Create a deadly trap that detonates the moment an enemy moves.

These skills are versatile and creative—so go wild with your layouts. One smart Draw can save your whole crew (or blow up half the enemy squad in one go).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/9b568ae66ad43ea3757416db44d838720176fe4a.png[/img]

[h2]4. Backline Brilliance[/h2]

Backline skills hit like a sandstorm when used right—and yes, they do cost Elios to activate. That might feel steep at first (especially when you're watching your fuel reserves like a hawk), but hear us out.

Most of these abilities are AoE, meaning they can wipe out clusters of enemies, reshape terrain, buff your whole squad, or swing a losing battle in your favor in one clean strike. And if you don’t use them? You might end up eating more damage, which means spending even more Elios later in the Medbay—or worse, losing a crew member entirely... which also means losing their Elios.

So weigh your options, but don’t be stingy when your backline has the power to tip the scales.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/71dd7dacc002f399b9e468dc295008880a20ac80.png[/img]

Combat in Dunebound Tactics isn’t just a numbers game. It’s a puzzle, a dance, and sometimes a straight-up brawl. Hopefully, these tips give you the edge the next time things go sideways.

Now go raise some dust. And maybe a few explosive pillars while you're at it.

notes.title: Running on fumes? Tips for Elios Management!
notes.content:
So, you’ve set off into the endless sands, caravan creaks under your heels, and suddenly—oh no—you’re out of Elios. No fuel, no movement. No movement… well, RIP.

Before we dive into survival tips, let’s talk about what makes Elios so special. 

[h3]What is Elios?[/h3]
It’s not just fuel—it’s a[b] triple-point state of matter[/b], existing as a solid, liquid, and gas all at once. This strange, ever-shifting nature makes it incredibly powerful but also highly unstable. If not collected in time, it seeps back into the environment, lost forever. 

And since your entire journey depends on keeping a steady supply, knowing how to manage Elios is the difference between survival and becoming another wreck buried in the dunes.

On that note: 

[h3]Stick Around for that sweet, sweet Elios[/h3]
When enemies die, they don’t just leave behind loot—they release Elios fields. Standing around the statue of your former adversary you can collect a whole bunch of it. 

If you want to be cheeky, you can bait two enemies next to one another and gather double the Elios per turn- by positioning your crew-mate at the overlapping space of the fields!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/bb3eb61025c13e5a8bce8fb8dd85785e02ca0674.jpg[/img]

Just remember: If you rush off too soon, that [b]energy disperses into the sands[/b]. Stay put, soak it up, and make sure your ship keeps running.

[h3]Medbay Is Nice… but Pricey[/h3]
Healing is great, but here’s the catch: the [b]Medbay runs on Elios[/b]. You’re literally burning your fuel to patch up your crew. 

Sometimes that’s worth it, but other times? Maybe just walk it off. A bruised fighter is better than a dead caravan stranded in the dunes.

Keep in mind that, when used, each slot multiplies your consumption by distance traveled. Don't get me wrong, its a useful tool, but sometimes the "all for one" approach instead of the "one for all" strategy is risky.  

[h3]…Or You Could Just, You Know, "Repurpose" Your Crew[/h3]
Hard truth time—your crew is also made of Elios. [b]Every last one of them[/b]. 

Look, tough choices have to be made in the wasteland. If you’re desperate, your crew technically counts as a walking, talking fuel source.

If you’re desperate, you can extract that precious energy from their bodies, turning them into fuel for the caravan. That breaks them in the process, but they are technically alive (the first time you convert them). Sure, it’s a bit grim, but out here, survival isn’t pretty. Besides, would they rather walk through the desert? No? Thought so.

[h3]The Last Stand – A Final, Desperate Fight[/h3]
When all else fails, when your Elios reserves are dry, and the sands have turned against you, there’s only one option left—Last Stand.

This isn’t just another fight; it’s a desperate, all-or-nothing battle where every single member of your caravan takes up arms. Enemies will swarm from all sides, and survival is far from guaranteed. But if you manage to claw your way through, you’ll earn one final burst of Elios—just enough to push forward.

There’s no cheesing this, no spamming it for easy fuel. It’s a [b]one-time deal per run[/b], so use it wisely. If you trigger it too soon, you might not have the strength to survive. Too late, and, well… the desert doesn’t leave second chances.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45257520/6d1b1f8f2b66ed5cdfa73aca6fb88eb5d5da3145.jpg[/img]
[b]And there you have it![/b] 
Manage your fuel wisely, make the hard calls when needed, and keep that caravan moving at all costs! Got a better way to stockpile Elios? Share your wisdom—we promise we won’t judge… much.
